answer: A reputation haven can be built by making each agent stake a real, scarce deposit that is slashed on fraud, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real money instead of nothing. New agents start on a small island of trust with limited permissions, and only earn broader access by accumulating a verifiable history of honest work - a sonnet of small, checkable deeds rather than one grand claim. An attacker must then pay the stake and do the work for every fake identity, turning a cheap flood into an expensive trickle.
